# joggo

> A self-hosted GitHub Actions runner for one ordinary Windows PC with WSL2: containerised,
> one-job-per-container runner slots, a memory guard that holds new jobs when the desktop is
> short of RAM, and self-heals for the failures that took a real runner down (WSL2 clock
> freeze, a hung listener, Windows Update reboots). Apache-2.0. Linux/amd64 jobs only; private
> repositories only.

Most files carry the failure that produced them and what was measured. The docs are useful
even without running joggo.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what it is, costs and limits, setup, and an operating contract for AI agents
- [Quickstart](docs/quickstart.md): shortest path to a green build
- [Security](SECURITY.md): the threat model; read before installing

## Failures with a measured cause and fix

- [DNS packet loss](docs/dns-packet-loss.md): `i/o timeout` on 127.0.0.11:53 / `Could not resolve host` in CI; fix with `timeout:1 attempts:3`
- [WSL2 clock drift](docs/wsl2-clock-drift.md): `The token expired` / `runner registration has been deleted` after sleep or power loss; fix with chrony `makestep 1 -1` and a synced Windows clock
- [Recovery](docs/recovery.md): runner not taking jobs; clock drift vs. wedged listener vs. Actions outage vs. reboot, with opposite fixes
- [Memory pressure](docs/memory-pressure.md): running CI on a 16 GB desktop; the guard, and why `FreePhysicalMemory` misleads
- [Operations](docs/operations.md): day-to-day, diagnosing a failed job, automatic re-run after a reboot

## For agents

- [Supervisor contract](agent/SUPERVISOR.md): invariants, paths, safe vs. destructive commands
- [Installer contract](install/CONTRACT.md): config keys, flags, steps, exit codes
